skill.name: psql
skill.description: Run PostgreSQL SQL, psql meta-commands, and SQL files from AI coding tools through a local CLI.
skill.summary: Run PostgreSQL queries, meta-commands, and SQL files from an AI coding session.
skill.author: Bind

security_audit.summary: Most external-command detections are Markdown syntax or command examples, not Ruby backtick execution. The skill still intentionally runs psql commands with configured credentials, so arbitrary database access and secret handling are the primary risks. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary SQL can read or modify configured databases.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running write queries, migrations, seed files, or administration commands.

remediation.issue: Database credentials may be stored in .env or exported environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend least-privilege accounts, read-only roles for inspection, and regular credential rotation.

remediation.issue: SQL file execution accepts local paths.
remediation.suggestion: Document that SQL files should come from trusted workspace paths and should be reviewed before execution.

remediation.issue: Production use can affect live data.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to verify the target database and backup status before production commands.

- Use `--tuples` for clean output without headers (useful for piping to other tools)
- Use `--json` for structured output when parsing programmatically

content.user_title: Query PostgreSQL from AI Coding Tools
content.value_statement: Database work often requires switching from an AI coding session to a terminal. This skill lets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code run PostgreSQL queries, meta-commands, and SQL files through psql.
actual_capabilities: Runs SQL queries through a local psql command.
Executes psql meta-commands for table and index inspection.
Runs SQL files for migrations or seed data.
Supports tuples-only output for script-friendly results.
Supports JSON-wrapped output and configurable query timeouts.
limitations: Requires Bun, psql, and PostgreSQL connection variables to be configured.
Does not keep a persistent database connection between queries.
Does not validate SQL intent before execution.
Can only reach databases available from the local environment.

use_cases.title: Inspect Database Schemas
use_cases.description: List tables, describe columns, and inspect indexes during application development.

use_cases.title: Run Operational Checks
use_cases.description: Check table sizes, active connections, and recent records during support work.

use_cases.title: Prepare Data Reports
use_cases.description: Run read-only aggregate queries and return terminal output for analysis.

prompt_templates.title: List Tables
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the psql skill to list tables in the configured database. Do not modify data.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Table
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the psql skill to describe the users table, then give a brief note about relevant columns.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Read-Only Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the psql skill to count recent orders by status for the last day. Keep the query read-only.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Migration File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the psql skill to run migrations/001_create_users.sql after I confirm the target database and backup status.

output_examples.output: The tool runs a psql table-listing command and returns the table names shown by psql.
The tool reports the current active connection count from PostgreSQL.
The tool executes the selected SQL file and shows the psql completion output.

best_practices: Use read-only database roles for inspection and reporting prompts.
Confirm the target database before running migrations or seed files.
Keep database credentials in trusted local configuration and rotate them regularly.
anti_patterns: Running prompts against production databases without a backup or approval.
Using privileged database accounts for routine schema exploration.
Pasting sensitive query results into unrelated conversations or public logs.

faq.question: Does this skill require PostgreSQL credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs PGHOST, PGDATABASE, PGUSER, and PGPASSWORD from the environment or a local .env file.

faq.question: Can it modify data?
faq.answer: Yes. It runs the SQL you provide, so write, migration, and seed commands can modify data.

faq.question: Does it validate SQL before running it?
faq.answer: No. Review every query and use least-privilege database roles.

faq.question: Can it run psql meta-commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports meta-commands such as listing tables, describing tables, and listing databases.

faq.question: Does it work without psql installed?
faq.answer: No. The local psql client and Bun runtime must be installed.

faq.question: Is it safe for production databases?
faq.answer: Use caution. Require confirmation, read-only roles, and backups before production use.
